def-additive-noise-model:
## Definition

Fix a nonempty finite directed acyclic graph $G=(V,E)$ with a specified
topological order $v_1,\ldots,v_p$; every arrow points from an earlier to a
later vertex. For $j\in V$, let
$\operatorname{pa}(j)=\{i\in V:(i,j)\in E\}$ be its parent set, and let
$\operatorname{nd}(j)$ be the vertices other than $j$ that are not descendants
of $j$. A **continuous additive-noise model** on $G$ consists of real random
variables $X_j,N_j$ on a common probability space and continuous Borel
functions $f_j:\mathbb R^{\operatorname{pa}(j)}\to\mathbb R$ such that
$$X_j=f_j(X_{\operatorname{pa}(j)})+N_j$$
recursively in the topological order. The finite family of noises is mutually
independent, and each $N_j$ has a strictly positive Lebesgue density $q_j$.
All vertices of $G$ are observed; no latent vertices are omitted from the
model. The **observational law** is the law of the vector
$X=(X_j)_{j\in V}$.

The model is **causally minimal** when every parent input is essential: for
each edge $i\to j$, there are values of the other parent coordinates and two
distinct real values of the $i$-coordinate at which $f_j$ takes different
values. A root has no parent-coordinate minimality condition.
lem-probability-measure-has-no-nonzero-p:
## Statement

Let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R$. If a real number
$a$ satisfies $\mu(A+a)=\mu(A)$ for every Borel set $A\subseteq\mathbb R$,
then $a=0$.
lem-smooth-residual-independence-has-poi:
## Statement

Let $C$ be a finite-dimensional real random vector, let $(Y,C)$ have a
strictly positive $C^3$ joint density $p(y,c)$, and let
$m:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ be $C^3$. If $R=Y-m(C)$ is independent of $C$, then there are
strictly positive $C^3$ Lebesgue density versions $q_R$ and $p_C$ such that
$$p(y,c)=q_R(y-m(c))p_C(c)$$
for every $(y,c)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$.
alg-resit:
## Definition

Fix a finite nonempty ordered vertex set $V$ and a population law of a real
vector $X=(X_j)_{j\in V}$ generated by an additive-noise model. A **population
regression rule** $\mathcal R$ assigns to each target $j\in V$ and predictor
set $C\subseteq V\setminus\{j\}$ a Borel function
$m_{j,C}:\mathbb R^C\to\mathbb R$. A **perfect independence oracle** returns
“independent” exactly when the tested random variable and random vector are
independent under this population law. For a given ANM, $\mathcal R$ is
**population-consistent on that model** if for every $j$ and every
$C$ with $\operatorname{pa}(j)\subseteq C\subseteq\operatorname{nd}(j)$,
there is a constant $c_{j,C}\in\mathbb R$ such that
$$m_{j,C}(X_C)=f_j(X_{\operatorname{pa}(j)})+c_{j,C}\quad\text{almost surely}.$$
This consistency condition concerns only the population regression target and
does not assert a finite-sample guarantee. The procedure itself is defined for
any supplied regression rule and oracle.

RESIT takes $X$, $\mathcal R$, and the perfect independence oracle and
performs the following steps, using a fixed total order on $V$ for every tie
and loop order.

1. Set the remaining set $S:=V$ and an empty sink list. While $S\ne\varnothing$,
   for each $j\in S$ form
   $$R_j:=X_j-m_{j,S\setminus\{j\}}(X_{S\setminus\{j\}}).$$
   Retain the vertices for which the oracle declares
   $R_j$ independent of $X_{S\setminus\{j\}}$. If there is no such vertex,
   return `failure`. Otherwise choose the least retained vertex $k$, record
   the provisional parent set $\widehat{\operatorname{pa}}(k):=S\setminus\{k\}$,
   append $k$ to the sink list, and remove $k$ from $S$.
2. Reverse the sink list to obtain an order $\pi$. In that order, for each
   vertex $j$ and each candidate $\ell$ in its provisional parent set, in the
   fixed order, let
   $C:=\widehat{\operatorname{pa}}(j)\setminus\{\ell\}$ and form
   $$R_{j,\ell}:=X_j-m_{j,C}(X_C).$$
   If the oracle declares $R_{j,\ell}$ independent of the vector of all
   vertices preceding $j$ in $\pi$, delete $\ell$ from
   $\widehat{\operatorname{pa}}(j)$; otherwise retain it.
3. Return the DAG with arrow $i\to j$ exactly when
   $i\in\widehat{\operatorname{pa}}(j)$ after pruning.
lem-anm-joint-density:
## Statement

Let a finite additive-noise model have topological order $v_1,\ldots,v_p$,
equations $X_j=f_j(X_{\operatorname{pa}(j)})+N_j$, and strictly positive
Lebesgue densities $q_j$ for its mutually independent noises. Write
$\lambda^{\otimes p}$ for the finite product of one-dimensional Lebesgue
measure. Then the observational law of $X=(X_j)_{j\in V}$ has the strictly
positive density
$$p_X(x)=\prod_{r=1}^p q_{v_r}\!\left(x_{v_r}-f_{v_r}(x_{\operatorname{pa}(v_r)})\right)$$
with respect to $\lambda^{\otimes p}$.
lem-anm-noise-independent-of-nondescenda:
## Statement

In a finite additive-noise model on a DAG $G$, for every vertex $j$ and every
set $S\subseteq\operatorname{nd}(j)$ of nondescendants, the noise $N_j$ is
independent of the random vector $X_S=(X_k)_{k\in S}$.
def-restricted-additive-noise-model:
## Definition

For a smooth bivariate additive-noise model $Y=f(X)+N$, let $f$ be three
times continuously differentiable, and let $X$ and $N$ have strictly positive
three-times continuously differentiable densities $p_X$ and $p_N$. Put
$\xi(x)=\log p_X(x)$ and $\nu(z)=\log p_N(z)$. The triple $(f,p_X,p_N)$
satisfies **Condition 19** when there are $x,y\in\mathbb R$ with
$\nu''(y-f(x))f'(x)\ne0$ at which
$$\xi'''(x)\ne \xi''(x)\left(-\frac{\nu'''(y-f(x))f'(x)}{\nu''(y-f(x))}+\frac{f''(x)}{f'(x)}\right) -2\nu''(y-f(x))f''(x)f'(x) +\nu'(y-f(x))f'''(x) +\frac{\nu'(y-f(x))\nu'''(y-f(x))f''(x)f'(x)}{\nu''(y-f(x))} -\frac{\nu'(y-f(x))(f''(x))^2}{f'(x)}.$$
Here every derivative of $\nu$ is evaluated at $y-f(x)$ and every derivative
of $f$ at $x$. The nonzero-domain condition makes both denominators in this
formula well defined.

A finite additive-noise model is a **restricted additive-noise model** when
every structural function $f_j$ is $C^3$ and every noise has a strictly
positive $C^3$ Lebesgue density, and when for every vertex $j$, every parent
$i\in\operatorname{pa}(j)$, and every set
$S$ satisfying
$$\operatorname{pa}(j)\setminus\{i\}\subseteq S\subseteq\operatorname{nd}(j)\setminus\{i\},$$
there is a value $s$ with $0<p_S(s)<\infty$ such that the
conditional law of $X_i$ given $X_S=s$, together with the structural slice
$u\mapsto f_j(s_{\operatorname{pa}(j)\setminus\{i\}},u)$ and the noise $N_j$,
is a smooth bivariate additive-noise model satisfying Condition 19. The
conditional density is the ratio
$p_{X_i,X_S}(u,s)/p_S(s)$ for the finite positive-density version supplied
by the joint-density formula. The structural slice and conditional input
density have the smoothness and strict positivity required in the preceding
Condition 19 definition. If the model has no edges, the restricted condition
is vacuous.
lem-anm-density-factorization-implies-ds:
## Statement

Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite DAG, and let $X$ follow a recursive additive-noise
model on $G$ in a fixed topological order, with continuous Borel structural
functions $f_v:\mathbb R^{\operatorname{pa}(v)}\to\mathbb R$ and equations
$$X_v=f_v(X_{\operatorname{pa}(v)})+N_v,$$
mutually independent noises with strictly positive Lebesgue densities $q_v$,
and joint density
$$p_X(x)=\prod_{v\in V}q_v\!\left(x_v-f_v(x_{\operatorname{pa}(v)})\right).$$
For $T\subseteq V$, let
$$p_T(x_T)=\int_{\mathbb R^{V\setminus T}}p_X(x)\,dx_{V\setminus T}$$
be the marginal density relative to finite product Lebesgue measure. Let
$A,B,C\subseteq V$ be pairwise disjoint with $A$ and $B$ nonempty. If $C$
d-separates $A$ and $B$ (every path from $A$ to $B$ has an internal
noncollider in $C$ or an internal collider with no descendant in $C$), then
$$p_{A\cup B\cup C}(x_A,x_B,x_C)p_C(x_C)=p_{A\cup C}(x_A,x_C)p_{B\cup C}(x_B,x_C)$$
for Lebesgue-almost every $(x_A,x_B,x_C)$. This identity is the
conditional-density factorization expressing conditional independence.
lem-anm-parent-dependence-persists-under:
## Statement

Let $X$ follow a finite additive-noise model with a strictly positive joint
density and continuous structural functions that are causally minimal in each
parent coordinate. For positive joint densities, write
$Y\perp_d A\mid Z$ when the conditional-density factorization
$$p_{Y,A,Z}(y,a,z)p_Z(z)=p_{Y,Z}(y,z)p_{A,Z}(a,z)$$
holds almost everywhere. For every edge $i\to j$ and every set $S$ such that
$$\operatorname{pa}(j)\setminus\{i\}\subseteq S\subseteq\operatorname{nd}(j)\setminus\{i\},$$
the density conditional-independence factorization
$X_j\perp_d X_i\mid X_S$ fails.
lem-youngest-child-descendants-condition:
## Statement

Let a finite causally sufficient additive-noise model have graph $G$, and let
$y\to z$ be an edge such that there is no directed path from $z$ to any other
child of $y$. Write $D=\operatorname{de}_G(z)$ for the strict descendants of
$z$ and $S=V\setminus(D\cup\{y,z\})$. If $p$ is the positive joint density,
there are positive measurable functions $A(y,s,z)$ and $B(d,s,z)$ such that
$p(d,y,s,z)=A(y,s,z)B(d,s,z)$, where $A$ does not depend on $d$ and $B$ does
not depend on $y$. Use marginal density versions obtained by iterated
integration. Then
$$p_{X_D,X_y,X_S,X_z}(d,y,s,z)\,p_{X_S,X_z}(s,z)=p_{X_D,X_S,X_z}(d,s,z)\,p_{X_y,X_S,X_z}(y,s,z)$$
for almost every $(d,y,s,z)$. This is the density conditional-independence
factorization of $X_D$ and $X_y$ given $(X_S,X_z)$. Moreover, for every $s$
with $0<p_{X_S}(s)<\infty$, the conditional law of $(X_D,X_y)$ given
$X_S=s$ satisfies the density conditional-independence factorization given
$X_z$.
lem-positive-minimal-dags-have-a-conditi:
## Statement

Let two finite causally sufficient additive-noise models on distinct DAGs
with the same vertex set have the same observational law, a strictly positive
joint density, and causal minimality in each model. If their DAGs are $G$ and $G'$, then there
are vertices $y,l$ and a set $S$ such that $y\to l$ in $G$, $l\to y$ in $G'$, and
$$\operatorname{pa}_G(l)\setminus\{y\}\subseteq S\subseteq \operatorname{nd}_G(l)\setminus\{y\},\qquad \operatorname{pa}_{G'}(y)\setminus\{l\}\subseteq S\subseteq \operatorname{nd}_{G'}(y)\setminus\{l\}.$$
thm-bivariate-additive-noise-identifiabi:
## Statement

Let $X,N$ be independent real random variables, let $Y=f(X)+N$, and suppose
$f\in C^3(\mathbb R)$ is nonconstant while $X$ and $N$ have strictly positive
$C^3$ Lebesgue densities. If the triple of $f$ and these two densities
satisfies Condition 19, then there is no reverse additive-noise representation
$X=g(Y)+M$ with $M$ independent of $Y$ and $g\in C^3(\mathbb R)$. No density
regularity for $M$ is assumed; the proof derives a strictly positive $C^3$
density version from the forward joint density and reverse independence. Hence
the direction $X\to Y$ is identified from the observational law among these
smooth bivariate additive-noise models.
thm-restricted-anm-population-identifica:
## Statement

Let a finite nonempty causally sufficient additive-noise model on a
DAG $G$ have a strictly positive joint density, be a restricted additive-noise
model, and be causally minimal. Then its observational law determines $G$
among all causally minimal restricted additive-noise models on the same
vertices.

For the population RESIT procedure, let $m_{j,C}:\mathbb R^C\to\mathbb R$ be
a supplied Borel regression rule and use an exact independence oracle and a
fixed total order for all ties and loops. Assume the rule is population
consistent on the model: whenever
$\operatorname{pa}(j)\subseteq C\subseteq\operatorname{nd}(j)$, there is a
constant $c_{j,C}$ such that
$$m_{j,C}(X_C)=f_j(X_{\operatorname{pa}(j)})+c_{j,C}\quad\text{almost surely}.$$
Assume in addition that every Phase 1 regression function $m_{j,C}$ is $C^3$
on its full predictor space. Then RESIT terminates without failure and returns
the DAG $G$. This is a population statement and makes no finite-sample claim.
